messages:
maria: quick heads-up — ran a 2h profile of the continuous-batcher with kernel-hinting enabled. saw a consistent spike in queue latency when KV hit rate drops below ~35%. attaching a couple of short logs and perf numbers below, want to sync on admission smoothing / soft-429 thresholds.
aj: can you drop the raw numbers? what token_budget target did you use and did you change batch formation window?
maria: token_budget_target=64 tokens/slot, batch_window=8ms, kernel_hint_policy=prefer-int8-for-seq<=512. extracted snippet: 
``
[run] 2024-10-03T14:02Z qlen=23 avg_lat=112ms kv_hit=29% token_budget_used=72
[run] 2024-10-03T14:03Z qlen=40 avg_lat=210ms kv_hit=28% soft_429=2
```
devon: hmm, 8ms batch window might be too tight. when kv hits fall we end up switching kernels more often; kernel-switch + serialization overhead looks like the culprit. did you capture kernel-switch latency?
maria: yes — kernel switch adds ~6–12ms per batch when we fall back to fp16 kernels. but the larger hit is smaller average batch sizes => higher per-batch overhead. profiler also shows idle time waiting on admission token refill spikes.
kai: suggestion — smooth the token budget refill: EMA over 5s on kv_hit and clamp changes to +/-20% per minute. add a probation/backoff for queues: instead of immediate soft-429, mark the queue as probation and allow 1 extra burst per 10s. reduces oscillation.
aj: can you sketch the config you tested? I can prototype flags in the runtime.
maria: quick draft config I tried: 
``
continuous_batching:
  batch_window_ms: 8
  token_budget_target: 64
  token_budget_smoothing_alpha: 0.2 # EMA
  token_budget_min_pct: 50
  token_budget_max_pct: 120
admission:
  soft_429_enabled: true
  soft_429_probation_window_s: 10
  soft_reject_threshold_qsz: 30
```
It improved average latency by ~14% during a 5–10% KV hit drop, but p95 still remained high.
perfbot: CI run 1722009905 completed — regression detected in continuous_batcher commit 9f3a — p95 +9% in stage env. tagging @maria @aj
devon: 9f3a touched kernel selection fallback order, right? if it prefers fp16 more often that would explain the regression and kernel-switch churn.
kai: action items: (1) add token budget EMA + clamp, (2) add probation flag with limited bursts, (3) instrument kernel-switch time per batch and expose metric to console. who owns which?
maria: I'll own 1 and 3. @aj can you take 2 (probation/backoff)? we'll run an A/B canary for 24h once prototypes are ready.
aj: got it. I'll open a small PR with probation_burst=1 per 10s default and a flag to tune. will post link here when ready.
maria: thanks. I'll also create a tiny eval prompt set that stresses low-kv-hit sequences to catch regressions earlier.
note: thread is a compact sync about profiling + admission heuristics; messages are chronological and short per slack style
